implementation_notes: A single KSerializer<T> object owns both directions - serialize(encoder, value) and deserialize(decoder) plus the descriptor that describes the encoded shape - and is attached with @Serializable(with = ...) or resolved through a SerializersModule, so the domain type and the wire format stay mutually unaware. Without the plugin, the dependency-free realization is a pair of extension or companion functions (fun toDto() / fun fromDto(dto: Dto)) or a @JvmInline value class with a format/parse pair; a converter class is justified only when one object must serve several types or formats.
pitfalls: The descriptor must agree with what serialize actually writes; a mismatch fails at runtime only on the real format.
A custom serializer bypasses the generated defaults, so a new constructor parameter is silently dropped until serialize/deserialize are updated.
For generated serializers, encodeDefaults and explicitNulls decide whether defaults travel on the wire; a hand-written serializer that always writes everything silently changes the contract.
KSerializer is format-agnostic and may be driven by Json, ProtoBuf or Cbor alike, so assumptions about text encoding inside it are invalid.
